subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A weak acid has Ka = 1.0 × 10⁻⁵ mol dm⁻³. Its pKa is:
questions.explain: pKa = −log Ka = −log(10⁻⁵) = 5.0.

questions.q: The enthalpy of atomisation of an element is the enthalpy change to form:
options: 1 mol of gaseous atoms from the element
questions.explain: Atomisation forms 1 mol of gaseous atoms from the element in its standard state.

questions.q: A reaction is predicted to be feasible under standard conditions when the calculated E°cell is:
options: equal to E° of the SHE
questions.explain: A positive E°cell corresponds to a negative ΔG, indicating a thermodynamically feasible reaction.

questions.q: For the reaction N2(g) + 3H2(g) → 2NH3(g), the sign of ΔS is:
options: Negative, gas moles decrease from 4 to 2
questions.explain: Moles of gas fall from 4 to 2, so disorder decreases and ΔS is negative.

questions.q: Which factors increase the magnitude (more exothermic) of a lattice enthalpy?
options: Larger ionic radii and smaller charges
Smaller ionic radii and larger ionic charges
questions.explain: Smaller, more highly charged ions give greater electrostatic attraction and a more exothermic lattice enthalpy.

questions.q: During electrolysis, the quantity of charge passed is given by:
questions.explain: Charge (coulombs) = current (amps) × time (seconds), Q = It.

questions.q: The purpose of the salt bridge in an electrochemical cell is to:
options: complete the circuit and maintain electrical neutrality
questions.explain: The salt bridge allows ions to flow to balance charge and complete the circuit; electrons flow through the wire.

questions.q: Disproportionation is a reaction in which a single species is:
questions.explain: In disproportionation one element in one oxidation state is both oxidised and reduced.

questions.q: The first electron affinity of a non-metal is usually:
questions.explain: Adding the first electron to a neutral gaseous atom releases energy, so it is exothermic.

questions.q: An oxidising agent is a species that:
options: donates electrons and is itself oxidised
accepts electrons and is itself reduced
questions.explain: An oxidising agent oxidises another species by accepting its electrons, so the agent is reduced.

questions.q: Which statement correctly defines the standard enthalpy of formation of a compound?
options: The enthalpy change when 1 mol of a compound is burned completely in oxygen
The enthalpy change when 1 mol of water is formed in a neutralisation reaction
The enthalpy change when 1 mol of a compound is formed from its elements in their standard states under standard conditions
The enthalpy change when 1 mol of gaseous atoms is formed from an element
questions.explain: ΔHf is defined as forming 1 mol of compound from its constituent elements in their standard states.

questions.q: The standard hydrogen electrode is assigned a standard electrode potential of:
questions.explain: By definition the SHE is the reference with E° = 0.00 V.

questions.q: For the cell Zn | Zn²⁺ || Cu²⁺ | Cu, the conventional cell representation places the:
options: salt bridge on the far left
more negative electrode (Zn) on the left
more positive electrode (Cu) on the left
questions.explain: By IUPAC convention the more negative (oxidation) half-cell is written on the left.

questions.q: In the conversion of Cr₂O₇²⁻ to Cr³⁺, chromium's oxidation number changes and it is:
questions.explain: Each Cr falls from +6 to +3 by gaining electrons, so it is reduced.

questions.q: What is the oxidation number of manganese in the permanganate ion, MnO₄⁻?
questions.explain: With O at −2 (×4 = −8) and overall charge −1, Mn must be +7.

questions.q: A catalyst is added to a system at equilibrium. What happens to the position of equilibrium?
options: It shifts towards the exothermic direction
questions.explain: A catalyst speeds up forward and reverse reactions equally, so it does not shift the equilibrium position.

questions.q: For an exothermic forward reaction, increasing the temperature will:
options: leave Kc unchanged but shift left
decrease Kc and shift equilibrium left
increase Kc and shift equilibrium right
questions.explain: Raising temperature favours the endothermic (reverse) direction, decreasing Kc and shifting equilibrium towards reactants.

questions.q: Which expression correctly represents Kp for 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g)?
questions.explain: Kp uses partial pressures of products over reactants each raised to its stoichiometric coefficient.

questions.q: Which is the correctly balanced half-equation for the oxidation of Fe²⁺ to Fe³⁺?
questions.explain: Losing one electron raises iron from +2 to +3, so Fe²⁺ → Fe³⁺ + e⁻.

questions.q: The Gibbs free energy change is given by:
questions.explain: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS.

questions.q: What is the oxidation number of hydrogen in the metal hydride NaH?
questions.explain: In metal hydrides hydrogen is −1 (the metal Na is +1).

questions.q: A reaction with ΔH < 0 and ΔS > 0 is:
questions.explain: With ΔH negative and ΔS positive, ΔG is negative at all temperatures.

questions.q: In the reaction Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu, the reducing agent is:
questions.explain: Zn loses electrons (is oxidised) and reduces Cu²⁺, so Zn is the reducing agent.

questions.q: In a Born–Haber cycle, the lattice enthalpy of formation refers to:
options: Breaking 1 mol of ionic lattice into gaseous ions
Forming 1 mol of ionic lattice from gaseous ions (exothermic)
questions.explain: Lattice enthalpy of formation is the exothermic formation of the lattice from gaseous ions.

questions.q: A strong monobasic acid differs from a weak monobasic acid because the strong acid:
options: has a larger Ka but does not fully dissociate
questions.explain: A strong acid is, by definition, fully (essentially completely) dissociated in aqueous solution.

questions.q: Using ΔHc (combustion data), the enthalpy of a reaction is calculated as:
questions.explain: With combustion data the cycle gives ΔHr = ΣΔHc(reactants) − ΣΔHc(products).

questions.q: What is the pH of a solution with [H⁺] = 1.0 × 10⁻³ mol dm⁻³?
What is the oxidation number of oxygen in hydrogen peroxide, H₂O₂?
questions.explain: In peroxides oxygen has the unusual oxidation number of −1.

questions.q: Which process is always exothermic?
questions.explain: Forming bonds releases energy, so bond making is exothermic.

questions.q: If 2 A flows for 965 seconds, how many moles of electrons pass? (F = 96500 C mol⁻¹)
